findings.message: The enabled host keeps ConfiguredJournalPort, which the verified implementation always makes fail; no sample journal port or host replacement is specified, so the March E2E flow cannot complete.

StartDemandRunHandler leaves ProcessingCutoffReference null, so DemandProcessor passes a run-specific fallback marker while SamplePreviousDemandPort accepts only the fixed sample marker; documented February arrears will not be loaded.
The host test asserts DemandRun CurrentDueTotal and ArrearsTotal, but the existing DemandProcessor only persists those totals on BillingSnapshot and does not populate the corresponding run fields.

SamplePreviousDemandPort does not verify persisted branch-scope sets, parent statuses/dimensions, complete cutoff/logical-scope linkage, or ownership of all tuple nodes, so it does not enforce the exact published historical tuple claimed by R6.
Task 3 ownership hashes cover only selected fields rather than every persisted fixture business field, so changes to omitted fields do not affect repair or the manifest fingerprint as required by R3.

Catalog and database validation are incomplete: required lookup/receipt uniqueness and invariants, complete mappings, foreign-key/linkage checks, historical counts/statuses, and aggregate equations are not all validated before commit.

Tasks 8 and 9 do not supply the acceptance-test coverage promised by the requirements and design, including deleted repair, both collision rollbacks, timestamp stability, all receipt rejection paths, full hierarchy, and exact previous-demand mutation cases.
The catalog contains only Tamil Nadu branches although the original request says in and around Tamil Nadu, and no assumption explains whether neighboring areas are intentionally excluded.

The configuration naming and authoring-boundary statements alternate between .config and .config.kiro, while both exist and R10 says only four artifacts are changed; the authoritative config and allowed-file count should be clarified.
